subtopics.title: How Individuals Put Pressure on Resources

questions.question: Which of these puts pressure on natural resources every day?
options: Everyday use of water, food, energy and goods by individuals

questions.question: In general, wealthier households:
options: Use far more resources than poorer households
Use fewer resources than poorer households
Use exactly the same as everyone

questions.question: About how much of the food produced in South Africa is lost or wasted?
Why are individual choices not made "in a vacuum"?
options: Because people have no choices at all
Because prices, services and what is available shape what people can choose

questions.question: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, which is called the:
A carbon footprint is:
options: The total greenhouse gases produced by a person's or group's activities
The amount of food a person eats

questions.question: Roughly how much carbon dioxide does an average South African produce from energy each year?
Why is South Africa's average carbon footprint high compared with most African countries?
options: Most of its electricity comes from coal and its industry uses a lot of energy
South Africa uses only solar power

subtopics.title: Practical Actions for Individuals and Households

questions.question: In the waste hierarchy, the first and best step is to:
options: Refuse or reduce what you do not need

questions.question: Which action saves electricity at home?
options: Using LED bulbs and switching off appliances
Using a tumble dryer every day
Boiling a full kettle for one cup

questions.question: During the Cape Town water crisis, residents were asked to use no more than:
Why does wasting less food help the environment?
options: It saves the land, water and energy used to produce food and reduces methane from landfills

subtopics.title: Individuals, Society and Government, and the Error Museum

questions.question: South Africa introduced a levy on plastic shopping bags in:
South Africa's carbon tax was introduced in:
Which statement is correct?
options: One person's actions make no difference
Recycling is always the most important step
A carbon footprint includes indirect emissions from electricity, food and goods
Individuals alone can solve climate change

questions.question: Why must governments and businesses act as well as individuals?
options: They control the largest sources of emissions and the systems people depend on

questions.question: In the Simplifier story, the "bucket with a hole" stands for:
Who usually has "bigger holes in their buckets"?
options: People with more money who use far more resources

questions.question: Cape Town's water use fell by about:
A carbon footprint is like:
options: A real shoe print in mud
An invisible mark that our activities leave on the air

questions.question: Carbon dioxide in the air acts like:
options: An ice cube cooling the earth

questions.question: Which activity adds to your carbon footprint?
options: Reading a printed book you already own

questions.question: Why do Americans have even bigger footprints than South Africans on average?
options: They use much more energy, transport and goods per person

questions.question: "Many hands make light work" means:
options: If everyone does a little, a lot gets done

questions.question: Which is a good habit for using fewer resources?
options: Taking a reusable bag to the shop
Leaving chargers on all the time

questions.question: Who must build clean power and safe public transport?
What is the main idea of this lesson?
options: Individuals can shrink their footprint, and it works best with action at every level
